lessons.title: Daily, Weekly, and Monthly Maintenance Checklists
lessons.body:
A solar pump for a dam is a big investment. To keep it running for 10 years or more, you need a simple routine. Start with daily checks. Every morning, before the pump starts, walk to the dam and look at the water level. If itâs too low, the pump may run dry and burn out. Check the pump house for leaks, unusual noises, or smoke. Look at the solar array â are any panels shaded by trees or dirt? Write down the water flow rate if you have a flow meter. A drop from 10,000 litres per hour to 8,000 means something is wrong. 

Weekly tasks take 30 minutes. Clean the panels with a soft brush and water â do this early morning when they are cool. Check all cables for cuts or loose connections. Inspect the pumpâs suction pipe for air leaks (youâll see bubbles). Test the controllerâs display â it should show voltage and current. If you have a backup generator, run it for 10 minutes. 

Monthly maintenance is more thorough. Grease the pump bearings if they have grease nipples â use a hand grease gun with lithium grease. Check the motorâs insulation resistance with a megohmmeter; it should be above 1 megohm. Tighten all bolts on the mounting frame. Clean the controllerâs cooling fins with a dry cloth. Test the float switch or dry-run protection by lifting it manually â the pump should stop. 

Keep a logbook. Record date, time, water flow, and any repairs. In Africa, dust and heat are hard on equipment. A simple checklist on a clipboard near the pump saves you from costly breakdowns. Train one person to do daily checks and another for weekly. Monthly, the whole team reviews the log. If you see the same problem three times, replace the part before it fails completely.

lessons.title: PV Module Cleaning and Inspection
lessons.body:
Dust, bird droppings, and leaves can cut your solar pumpâs power by 30% or more. In dry African regions, panels need cleaning every week during the dry season. Use a soft sponge or cloth and plain water â never use soap or abrasive cleaners. Clean early morning or late afternoon when panels are cool; cold water on hot glass can crack it. For a 3 kW array, youâll need about 20 litres of water. If water is scarce, use a dry microfibre cloth, but be gentle to avoid scratches. 

Inspect panels for cracks, hot spots, and loose frames. Walk along the array and look at each panel. A cracked panel still works but may fail soon. Check the junction box underneath â look for burnt wires or water inside. Tighten the cable glands. Test the open-circuit voltage of each string with a multimeter. For a 24V system, each panel should read about 36V open-circuit. If one reads 20V, itâs faulty. 

Shading is a killer. Even a small branch casting a shadow on one cell can reduce the whole stringâs output. Trim trees 3 metres away from the array. If you have a ground-mounted array, keep grass short. After cleaning, check that all mounting bolts are tight â use a spanner and tighten to 15 Nm. 

Record your cleaning in a log. Note the date, weather, and any damage. In the rainy season, rain cleans panels, but dust can turn to mud. After a dust storm, clean immediately. A clean array can increase water pumping by 20-30%, paying for your time. Teach a local youth to do this weekly â itâs a simple job that protects the whole system.

lessons.title: Pump and Motor Maintenance
lessons.body:
The pump and motor are the heart of your solar pump system. For a submersible pump in a dam, you need to check it every month. First, turn off the power. Lift the pump out of the water if possible â or use a rope to feel for vibration. Check the impeller for wear. Sand and grit wear down impellers fast. If the impeller is worn, water flow drops. Replace it every 2 years in sandy dams. 

Check the motor windings with a multimeter. Set it to ohms. Measure between each terminal and the motor body. You should get infinite resistance (no continuity). If you get a reading, the winding is shorted to ground â the motor is dead. Also measure between terminals: for a 3-phase motor, all three readings should be equal. If one is different, the winding is damaged. 

Lubricate the motor bearings if they have grease nipples. Use a grease gun with high-temperature lithium grease. Two pumps of grease per bearing every 3 months. Over-greasing can blow seals. Check the mechanical seal for leaks. A few drops per hour is normal, but a steady stream means replace the seal. 

For surface pumps, check the belt tension â it should deflect 1 cm with thumb pressure. Tighten or replace belts. Clean the motorâs cooling fan and fins. In Africa, heat is the enemy. Ensure the pump house has ventilation. If the motor is too hot to touch (above 60Â°C), stop it and find the cause. 

Keep spare impellers, seals, and bearings on site. A pump failure during irrigation season can cost you a harvest. Train a local technician to do these checks. Record all maintenance in a logbook. If the pump runs dry, it can burn out in minutes â always have a dry-run protection sensor.

lessons.title: Controller and Inverter Maintenance
lessons.body:
The controller is the brain of your solar pump. It manages power from the panels to the pump. For an inverter (if you use AC pump), it converts DC to AC. Both need regular care. Every week, look at the controllerâs display. It should show input voltage (e.g., 300V DC) and output current. If the display is blank, check the fuses. Most controllers have a 10A fuse on the input. Replace with the same rating â never use a bigger fuse. 

Clean the controllerâs cooling fins with a dry brush. Dust blocks airflow and causes overheating. In hot African climates, mount the controller in a shaded, ventilated box. If it feels hot, add a small 12V fan. Check all cable connections â tighten the screws on the terminal block. Loose connections cause arcing and fire. Use a screwdriver to snug them every month. 

For inverters, check the error codes. A red light means fault. Common codes: âOvervoltageâ â too many panels in series; âUndervoltageâ â low sun or dirty panels; âOverloadâ â pump jammed. Reset by turning off for 5 minutes. If the fault returns, call a technician. Test the inverterâs output voltage with a multimeter â it should be 230V AC Â±10%. 

Check the surge protector. If it has a window that turned black, replace it. In lightning-prone areas, a surge protector saves your inverter. Also check the grounding rod â it should be copper, 2 metres deep, with a tight clamp. Measure resistance to earth; it should be under 5 ohms. 

Keep a spare controller or inverter if you can afford it. A failed controller can stop pumping for weeks. Log all faults and fixes. If the controller fails often, check for voltage spikes from the pump. Add a soft starter if needed.

lessons.title: Monitoring Systems and Remote Diagnostics
lessons.body:
You cannot be at the dam every day. Monitoring systems let you check your pump from your phone. Basic systems use a GSM module that sends SMS alerts. For example, if the pump stops, you get a text: âPump fault â dry run.â Cost: about $100. Install a SIM card with data. Set alerts for low water level, low voltage, and high motor temperature. 

More advanced systems use a small computer (like a Raspberry Pi) with sensors. Measure water flow with a pulse flow meter â each pulse equals 1 litre. Measure current with a clamp meter. Send data to a free cloud service like ThingSpeak. You can see graphs of daily water output. If flow drops by 20%, you know maintenance is needed. 

Remote diagnostics means checking the system without going there. Use a smartphone app to see live voltage, current, and power. If the voltage is 0, the panels are dirty or a fuse blew. If current is high but flow is low, the pump is clogged. You can also reset the controller remotely if it has that feature. 

In Africa, network coverage can be poor. Use a system that stores data locally and sends when signal is available. A simple data logger with an SD card costs $50. Download data weekly. Look for patterns: pump starts late? Panels shaded. Pump stops at noon? Overheating. 

Train a local operator to read the SMS alerts. If they get âdry run,â they should check the dam level and reset the controller. For remote areas, pair with a neighbour who can check the pump. Monitoring saves fuel and time â you only visit when needed. Keep the SIM card charged with airtime. Test the system monthly by simulating a fault.

lessons.title: Spare Parts Management and Inventory
lessons.body:
A solar pump without spare parts is a dead pump. In rural Africa, waiting for a part from the city can take weeks. You need a minimum inventory. Start with these: 2 spare PV panels (same model), 1 spare controller, 1 spare pump impeller, 1 set of seals, 10 metres of cable, 5 fuses (10A and 20A), 1 float switch, and 1 set of bearings. For a 3 kW system, this costs about $800. Itâs insurance. 

Store parts in a dry, cool room. Heat and humidity destroy electronics. Keep controllers in their original anti-static bags. Put desiccant packets in the box. Label everything with a marker â âController 24Vâ etc. Keep a logbook of parts used. When you take a fuse, write the date and reason. 

Order new parts before you run out. Set a reorder level: when you have only 2 fuses left, order 10 more. Use a simple inventory sheet: part name, quantity, minimum, date ordered. Check inventory monthly. In the rainy season, you may need more spare cables due to lightning damage. 

Buy local when possible. A local welder can make a pump stand. A motor rewinding shop in town can fix a burnt motor. But for controllers and panels, buy from a reputable solar supplier. Fake panels lose power in 6 months. Keep receipts for warranty. Most panels have 10-year warranty, controllers 2 years. 

Train one person as storekeeper. They sign out parts. If a part fails often, investigate why. Maybe the pump is oversized. Share spares with neighbouring farms â a cooperative can buy a shared inventory. That reduces cost. Never cannibalise a working pump for parts. Keep your spare pump ready to swap in 1 hour. Thatâs how you keep water flowing.

quiz.q: What should you check daily on a solar pump system?
options: A) Water level and flow rate
quiz.explanation: Daily checks include water level and flow rate to catch problems early.

quiz.q: How often should you clean PV modules in dry African regions?
quiz.explanation: Weekly cleaning is needed during dry season to prevent dust buildup.

quiz.q: What is the correct way to clean solar panels?
options: B) Use a soft brush and plain water
quiz.explanation: Soft brush and plain water avoid scratches and damage.

quiz.q: What should you do if a PV panel reads 20V open-circuit when it should be 36V?
quiz.explanation: Low voltage indicates a faulty panel that needs replacement.

quiz.q: Why is shading on solar panels a problem?
options: B) It reduces output of the whole string
quiz.explanation: Even small shade can significantly reduce power output.

quiz.q: What tool is used to check motor winding insulation?
quiz.explanation: Megohmmeter measures insulation resistance above 1 megohm.

quiz.q: How often should you grease pump bearings with grease nipples?
quiz.explanation: Greasing every 3 months is typical for pump bearings.

quiz.q: What indicates a mechanical seal leak in a pump?
options: A) A few drops per hour
quiz.explanation: A steady stream means the seal needs replacement.

quiz.q: What is the maximum allowable temperature for a motor before stopping?
quiz.explanation: If motor is above 60Â°C, stop it to prevent damage.

quiz.q: What should you do if a controller display is blank?
quiz.explanation: A blank display often means a blown fuse.

quiz.q: What does an inverter error code 'Overvoltage' mean?
options: A) Too many panels in series
quiz.explanation: Overvoltage occurs when input voltage exceeds inverter limits.

quiz.q: How often should you tighten controller terminal screws?
quiz.explanation: Monthly tightening prevents loose connections and arcing.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a surge protector?
quiz.explanation: Surge protectors divert excess voltage from lightning.

quiz.q: What should grounding rod resistance be?
quiz.explanation: Good grounding requires less than 5 ohms resistance.

quiz.q: What is a simple monitoring system for a solar pump?
quiz.explanation: GSM modules send SMS alerts for faults.

quiz.q: What does a pulse flow meter measure?
quiz.explanation: Each pulse represents a volume of water, measuring flow.

quiz.q: What does it mean if current is high but flow is low?
quiz.explanation: High current with low flow indicates a clogged or jammed pump.

quiz.q: How often should you test remote monitoring system?
quiz.explanation: Monthly testing ensures alerts work when needed.

quiz.q: What is a minimum spare part for a solar pump?
quiz.explanation: Impellers wear out and are critical spares.

quiz.q: How should you store spare controllers?
options: B) In anti-static bags with desiccant
quiz.explanation: Anti-static bags and desiccant protect electronics.

quiz.q: What is a reorder level?
quiz.explanation: Reorder level triggers new order when stock drops to that point.

quiz.q: Why keep a logbook for maintenance?
options: A) To record repairs and patterns
quiz.explanation: Logbooks help track recurring issues and plan maintenance.

quiz.q: What should you do if the same problem occurs three times?
quiz.explanation: Repeated problems indicate a failing part that should be replaced.

quiz.q: What is the recommended grease for pump bearings?
quiz.explanation: Lithium grease is suitable for high-temperature bearings.

quiz.q: How often should you check the pump's suction pipe for air leaks?
quiz.explanation: Weekly checks catch air leaks that reduce pump efficiency.

quiz.q: What is a dry-run protection sensor for?
options: A) Prevent pump running without water
quiz.explanation: Dry-run protection stops pump if water level is too low.

quiz.q: What should you do before cleaning solar panels?
quiz.explanation: Turning off pump prevents accidental startup during cleaning.

quiz.q: What is the typical open-circuit voltage of a 24V solar panel?
quiz.explanation: A 24V nominal panel has about 36V open-circuit.

quiz.q: Why is ventilation important for pump house?
quiz.explanation: Ventilation prevents motor overheating in hot climates.

quiz.q: What should you do if inverter shows 'Overload' error?
quiz.explanation: Overload may be temporary; reset and check for jammed pump.
